candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: administer medications safely, calculate/verify doses, monitor response, and provide medication teaching.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin degludec administration
candidate.educational_objective: Teach adult insulin degludec administration as once-daily subcutaneous dosing with individualized titration and no manual dose conversion between FlexTouch U-100 and U-200 pens.

options.A: Inject insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily; adults may administer it at any time of day, while the dose should still be individualized to metabolic needs and glucose-control goals.
options.B: Inject insulin degludec only by intravenous infusion because subcutaneous administration is not labeled.
options.C: Administer insulin degludec only immediately before meals because its labeled role is rapid prandial glucose control.
options.D: Convert the displayed units when using U-100 versus U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window does not show the actual insulin units.

candidate.rationale: Current TRESIBA labeling instructs adults to inject insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily at any time of day and to individualize/titrate the dose based on metabolic needs, blood-glucose monitoring results, and glycemic goals. The label also states not to perform dose conversion between U-100 and U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window displays the number of units to deliver. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Adults use insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily at any time of day with individualized dosing; FlexTouch U-100/U-200 pens do not require manual dose conversion.
candidate.source_locator: §2.1 Important Administration Instructions and §2.2 General Dosing Instructions: subcutaneous administration; adults once daily at any time of day; pediatric patients same time every day; individualize/titrate dose; no dose conversion between U-100/U-200 FlexTouch pens.
